headline: Nasdaq-100 weekend halt: Tail stays low after Friday's record probe was fully retraced, while a long end near multi-decade highs, triple-digit Brent and fresh Gulf escalation reports keep Stress elevated
body: Friday closed the Nasdaq-100 at 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% and a record close, after probing an intraday record of 31,017.53 and then giving back roughly 210 points to finish near the session low of 30,737.07. That completed retracement is the last observable price path before CME equity-index futures halted at 21:00Z, and it is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that this framework treats as Tail evidence. Every hour of the published forecast window falls inside that halt, which does not end until the Sunday restart at 22:00Z, beyond this horizon. The session was driven by a soft September employment report: 29,000 jobs added against roughly 90,000 expected, unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 0.1% month over month. Bond traders cut October rate-hike odds to about 16% from roughly 64% a week earlier, and technology led, with Nvidia up more than 2% to an intraday record of $237.87 and Tesla up about 4% on 486,532 third-quarter deliveries against a 463,000 consensus. The VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59%, on a 15.30 to 16.24 range, so there is no observed volatility expansion to carry into the weekend. The rate channel is less supportive than the equity close implies and the evidence is genuinely mixed here. Reporting immediately after the payroll release described the 10-year falling about six basis points to 5.18% and the 2-year to 4.73%, but the Trading Economics quote feed records the 10-year ending 2 October near 5.283%, up about four basis points, with the 2-year at 4.84% and the 30-year at 5.61%, after the 10-year had earlier climbed above 5.34%, its highest since 2002. Read together, Friday's post-payroll bond rally appears to have faded into the close, so the long end did not confirm the equity advance. That unresolved cross-asset conflict is treated here as a Stress and Confidence input rather than as Tail evidence. Brent trades near $102.25, up roughly 7% on the month, and the G7 has agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude stocks over four months. Middle Eastern crude exports have recovered close to pre-war levels at about 21.8 million barrels per day against 23.3 million before the war, but refined-product flows through Hormuz remain near 677,000 barrels per day against roughly 3.6 million pre-war, and China has halted most refined fuel exports for October. The geopolitical channel firmed on Saturday. A Tehran source said Iran is preparing for a major round of fighting, the USS Theodore Roosevelt is en route as a third carrier strike group alongside an amphibious group carrying about 2,000 Marines, and a crude tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile roughly four nautical miles off Oman. Against that, no coalition strikes on Iranian territory have been reported for twenty-six consecutive operational periods, Iran has launched no ballistic missiles for twenty-four days and no drone attacks for twenty-eight days, and President Trump indicated any renewed strikes would more likely follow the 3 November midterms. Under this framework that escalation raises Stress and bears on Confidence; it does not raise Tail while there is no session in which a pathological path could develop. Confidence is 85 and eases through the window as Friday's evidence ages, with a modest deduction for the conflicting Treasury readings. The shared Finviz context file was not usable for this run: its collection status is partial and its collection time of 29 September is roughly four days old, far outside the 90-minute freshness window, so it was disregarded and the assessment rests on independently verified primary sources. Dominant mode is recorded as normal, describing an orderly two-way close followed by a halted market rather than any directional regime. A Sunday OPEC+ online meeting, expected to hold November production targets unchanged, is the one scheduled catalyst close to this window, though the decision and the restart that would price it both fall after the final published hour.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the back half of Friday's payroll session and the first fifteen hours of the weekend halt. Tail stood at 24 into the 12:30Z payroll release and reached 25 and then 27 across the 13:30Z cash open as the index gapped higher and extended toward its intraday record, the only stretch of the window that produced an orange state. Once that advance stalled and price retraced roughly 210 points into a close near the session low, Tail fell back to 22 and held between 21 and 23 through the U.S. afternoon. After the 21:00Z futures halt it dropped to 14 and then decayed steadily to 4 by the 11:00Z hour as the absence of a tradeable session removed the mean-reversion-failure mechanism. Stress fell from 79 at the cash open to 55 by the end of the window as volatility decayed, and dominant mode moved from trend-up during the opening extension to mixed and then normal once the halt began. Confidence stayed between 82 and 89 throughout. All 24 slots are backed by published Claude assessments and are reproduced here without hindsight revision.
outlookSummary: All 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt: index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, beyond this horizon. With no tradeable session there is no mechanism for sustained mean-reversion failure, so Tail is projected to hold between 3 and 4 and every hour maps to EA_ON and green. Stress eases from 54 to a window low of 50 overnight and then firms back to 57 by the final hour as unabsorbed weekend inputs accumulate: a Sunday OPEC+ online meeting expected to hold November targets unchanged, Saturday reports that Iran is preparing for a major round of fighting, a tanker struck off Oman, triple-digit Brent and a Treasury long end that closed higher despite a weak payroll print. Every projected hour stays in the elevated Stress band. Confidence declines from 85 to 78 to reflect Friday's closing evidence ageing across a weekend in which no new price path can be observed, conflicting Treasury readings for 2 October, and an unusable shared Finviz context file. Hour-specific notes mark the Friday session analogues, the weekend escalation reports, the Sunday OPEC+ checkpoint and the Treasury supply stack; the nearest scheduled U.S. releases, Monday's ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z and Wednesday's FOMC Minutes at 18:00Z, sit outside this window and are carried in the event calendar.
